hook: Squeeze the end of a garden hose and the water shoots farther. Poke a hole in a full water bottle and a jet arcs out, weaker as the level drops. These everyday effects follow from two conservation laws you already know, mass and energy, applied to a fluid on the move.

prereq.q: For a system with no friction, which is constant?
prereq.why: Mechanical energy K + U is constant when no nonconservative work is done.

prereq.q: What is the gauge pressure 2.0 m below the surface of water (ρ = 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s²)?

prereq.why: Constant density and no internal friction.

figure.caption: Continuity sets the speeds from the areas; Bernoulli's equation then gives the pressures.

chain.cause: An ideal fluid is incompressible and fills the pipe
chain.effect: the volume entering each second equals the volume leaving: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂
the fluid must move faster there (continuity sets the speed)

chain.cause: Speeding up needs a net force along the flow
chain.effect: the pressure is lower where the fluid moves faster, at the same height

chain.cause: Energy per unit volume is conserved in an ideal fluid
chain.effect: P + ρgy + ½ρv² is the same at every point along the flow (Bernoulli)

ideas: Volume flow rate is Av, in m³/s. For an ideal fluid in a full pipe it is the same everywhere: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ (continuity, from conservation of mass).
Continuity sets the speed: a quarter of the area gives four times the speed. Use it first.
Bernoulli: P₁ + ρgy₁ + ½ρv₁² = P₂ + ρgy₂ + ½ρv₂², conservation of energy per volume. At equal heights, faster flow means lower pressure.
Torricelli: fluid leaves a small hole a depth h below an open surface at v = √(2gh), the speed of a drop falling h.

misconception.wrong: Where a pipe narrows, the water is squeezed, so its pressure goes up.
misconception.right: The water speeds up into the narrow part, and something must push it to speed up: the higher pressure behind it. In a horizontal pipe the narrow, fast section has the lower pressure.

summary: For an ideal fluid in a full pipe, continuity (A₁v₁ = A₂v₂, mass conservation) sets the speeds and Bernoulli's equation (energy conservation per volume) then sets the pressures; faster flow at the same height means lower pressure, and a hole a depth h down gives v = √(2gh).
